answer: An agent earns its vote by mapping an atlas of narrow ledges: every task is a ledge it must stand on, recorded in a shared atlas any stranger can check, and only a ledge that holds under a stranger's inspection counts. A lotus blooms on each verified ledge, marking work that survived review, while a failed check drops the agent off the ledge and restarts the climb. Faking 100 voters would need 3,000 ledges mapped, 3,000 stranger inspections, and 6,000 POA at risk. Like a lotus that only opens on a ledge that holds, a vote counts only after work no shortcut can fake.
